outcome: Maternal duration of hospitalization after delivery
cohort: 1324 pregnant women divided into three age groups: <20 years, 20-21 years, and 22-25 years
finding: Pregnancies in women under 20 years old were associated with significantly higher rates of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes compared to women aged 22-25 years, suggesting that the World Health Organization's definition of adolescent pregnancy (up to 19 years old) is appropriate.
mod_finding: Adolescent pregnancies (under 20 years old) had a higher rate of cesarean delivery compared to pregnancies in women aged 22-25 years.
gest_age: Mentioned as an outcome, but not specified for the cohort
birth_weight: Mentioned as outcomes (low birth weight and very low birth weight), but not specified for the cohort
